title: Encoded PowerShell Command Line
description: Detects PowerShell launched with Base64 encoded commands, hidden windows or no-profile flags — a staple of initial execution and loader staging.
author: PKC Research
query:
// Defender for Endpoint / Sentinel
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-EncodedCommand", "-enc ", "-e ", "FromBase64String", "-nop", "-w hidden", "-windowstyle hidden")
| project Timestamp, AccountName, DeviceName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

title: New Scheduled Task Registration
description: Finds non-Microsoft scheduled tasks created via Event 4698. Review the task action binary path and creator account.
author: PKC Research
query:
index=wineventlog sourcetype=WinEventLog:Security EventCode=4698
| table _time, Computer, SubjectUserName, TaskName, TaskContent
| where NOT like(TaskName, "%\\Microsoft\\Windows\\%")
| rex field=TaskContent "<Command>(?<action>[^<]+)</Command>"
| stats count as creations, values(action) as actions, values(SubjectUserName) as creators by Computer, TaskName
| where count > 0
| sort - creations

title: Rare Parent-Child Process Pair
description: Surfaces parent/child process relationships that occur in fewer than 0.5% of hosts — a strong signal for LOLBin abuse and shell spawning.
author: PKC Research
query:
// Requires >= 14 days of EndpointEvents baseline
let baseline = DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d) and Timestamp < ago(1d)
| summarize pair_count = count() by InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| join kind=leftanti baseline on InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName
| summarize events = count(), devices = dcount(DeviceName) by InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName
| where devices <= 3
| sort by events desc

title: Outbound Beaconing to Rare Domains
description: Classic beacon detection: low jitter, regular intervals and destinations rarely seen in the environment.
author: PKC Research
query:
index=proxy status=200
| where isnotnull(dest_domain)
| bin _time span=5m
| stats count as hits, dc(dest_domain) as dests by src_ip, dest_domain
| join type=left [search index=proxy earliest=-30d latest=-1d
  | stats dc(_time) as observed_windows by src_ip, dest_domain
  | where observed_windows < 5]
| eval regularity = round(hits / 1.0, 2)
| where hits >= 12 and dests <= 2
| sort - hits

title: LSASS Handle Access from Unsigned Binary
description: Sigma-style rule catching credential dumpers opening LSASS with PROCESS_VM_READ from anything other than a signed Microsoft binary.
author: PKC Research
query:
title: Suspicious LSASS Handle Access
id: 7f2c1f4e-6c1a-4a51-9d3b-0f4b6d2a1c99
description: Detects non-Microsoft processes requesting read access to LSASS memory
status: experimental
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Project KillChain Hub
date: 2026-01-15
logsource:
  category: process_access
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetImage|endswith: '\\lsass.exe'
    GrantedAccess|contains:
      - '0x1010'
      - '0x1410'
  filter:
    SourceImage|startswith:
      - 'C:\\Windows\\System32\\'
      - 'C:\\Program Files\\Windows Defender\\'
  condition: selection and not filter
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate EDR and debugging tooling
level: high
tags:
  - attack.credential_access

title: Office Application Spawned a Shell
description: Word, Excel or PowerPoint launching cmd/powershell/mshta — the classic malicious document execution path.
author: PKC Research
query:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("WINWORD.EXE", "EXCEL.EXE", "POWERPNT.EXE", "OUTLOOK.EXE", "MSACCESS.EXE")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "mshta.exe", "wscript.exe", "cscript.exe", "rundll32.exe", "regsvr32.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

title: MFA Push Fatigue (Repeated Denials)
description: Flags accounts receiving a burst of denied MFA pushes — the tell-tale sign of push-bombing social engineering.
author: PKC Research
query:
// Microsoft Entra ID sign-in logs
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ResultType in ("50126", "50074", "50076", "50079")
| summarize pushes = count(),
              first_denial = min(TimeGenerated),
              last_denial = max(TimeGenerated),
              apps = make_set(AppDisplayName, 10)
        by UserPrincipalName, IPAddress
| where pushes >= 5
| extend interval_minutes = datetime_diff('minute', last_denial, first_denial)
| where interval_minutes <= 30
| sort by pushes desc

title: DNS Tunnelling Heuristics
description: Detects unusually long or high-entropy DNS queries indicative of data exfiltration over DNS.
author: PKC Research
query:
index=dns
| eval qname_len = len(query)
| eval label_len = strlen(mvindex(split(query, "."), 0))
| where qname_len > 60 or label_len > 40
| stats avg(qname_len) as avg_len, max(qname_len) as max_len,
        count as queries, dc(query) as unique_queries,
        values(src) as sources
        by dest, query
| eval uniq_ratio = round(unique_queries / queries, 2)
| where queries >= 10
| sort - avg_len

title: Microsoft Defender Real-Time Protection Disabled
description: Sigma rule for tamper events where real-time monitoring, behavior monitoring or IOAV protection is switched off.
author: PKC Research
query:
title: Microsoft Defender Protection Disabled
id: 3c9d1a72-88bb-4d5f-9a0e-2f6c7b54e118
description: Detects events indicating Microsoft Defender real-time protection was disabled
status: stable
author: Project KillChain Hub
date: 2026-02-02
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: mdefender
detection:
  selection:
    EventID:
      - 5001
      - 1116
      - 1006
    Keyword|contains:
      - 'RTP disabled'
      - 'real-time protection'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Planned administrative changes
level: medium
tags:
  - attack.defense_evasion

title: Anomalous RDP Logons Between Workstations
description: Workstation-to-workstation RDP logons are rare in most environments and common in lateral movement.
author: PKC Research
query:
index=wineventlog sourcetype=WinEventLog:Security (EventCode=4624 OR EventCode=4778) Logon_Type=10
| stats count as sessions, values(TargetUserName) as accounts by src, dest
| where NOT like(src, "10.%") OR NOT like(dest, "10.%")
| join type=left [search index=cmdb sourcetype=asset
  | eval is_workstation = if(itype="workstation", 1, 0)
  | table host, is_workstation]
| where is_workstation=1
| sort - sessions

title: Fake Browser Update Lure (YARA)
description: YARA rule for the injected script pattern used by fake-update (ClickFix style) landing pages served from hijacked WordPress sites.
author: PKC Research
query:
rule Fake_Update_Lure_Script
{
  meta:
    description = "Fake browser update / ClickFix landing page script"
    author = "Project KillChain Hub"
    date = "2026-03-01"
    reference = "educational-defensive-rule"
  strings:
    $a = "Your browser is out of date" ascii nocase
    $b = "Press Win + R" ascii nocase
    $c = "update.js?build=" ascii nocase
    $d = "document.execCommand('copy')" ascii nocase
    $e = "chrome://settings" ascii nocase
  condition:
    filesize < 512KB and 3 of ($*)
}

title: Mass File Rename Consistent with Ransomware
description: Detects a single host renaming hundreds of files across user profiles in a short window — encryptor behaviour.
author: PKC Research
query:
FileCreationEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where ActionType = "FileRenamed"
| summarize renamed = count(),
            extensions = make_set(RenameTargetFileExtension, 8),
            folders = dcount(FolderPath)
        by DeviceName, AccountName
| where renamed >= 250 and folders >= 5
| sort by renamed desc

title: Service Installation via sc.exe or PowerShell
description: New services are a durable persistence mechanism. This hunt isolates service installs created from user-writable paths.
author: PKC Research
query:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FileName in~ ("sc.exe", "services.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has "create")
    or (FileName =~ "powershell.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("New-Service", "sc.exe create"))
| extend bin = extract(@"binPath(?:\s*=\s*|\s+)(?<b>[^\s]+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
| where isnotempty(bin) and (bin has "\\Users\\" or bin has "\\Temp\\" or bin has "\\AppData\\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, bin
| order by Timestamp desc

title: PowerShell Download Cradle
description: Catches Invoke-WebRequest / Net.WebClient download patterns used to fetch second-stage payloads.
author: PKC Research

title: Kerberoasting: Unusual Service Ticket Requests
description: Accounts requesting service tickets for many SPNs in a short window, especially from non-server accounts.
author: PKC Research
query:
index=wineventlog sourcetype=WinEventLog:Security EventCode=4769
| where ServiceName NOT IN ("krbtgt", "*")
| eval spn = ServiceName
| stats count as tickets, dc(spn) as distinct_spns, values(spn) as spns by Account_Name, src
| where tickets >= 10 and distinct_spns >= 5
| join type=left [search index=cmdb sourcetype=asset | table host, role]
| where role != "domain_controller"
| sort - tickets

title: Suspicious Child of Winword with Network Connection
description: Chains process and network telemetry: documents that both spawn interpreters and open outbound connections.
author: PKC Research
query:
let proc = DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("WINWORD.EXE", "EXCEL.EXE", "POWERPNT.EXE")
| project proc_time = Timestamp, DeviceName, child = FileName, child_cmd = ProcessCommandLine;
let net = DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIPType = "Public" and ActionType = "ConnectionAllowed"
| project net_time = Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName;
proc
| join kind=inner net on DeviceName
| where datetime_diff('minute', net_time, proc_time) between (0 .. 30)
| summarize connections = make_set(RemoteUrl, 10), first_seen = min(proc_time) by DeviceName, child, child_cmd
| sort by first_seen desc
